rationale: This is a sign-flipped, cosmetically re-parameterized (3-year TREND vs 1-year DELTA) restatement of the archived "Balance Sheet Repair Weighted Value," with the positive expected sign reverse-engineered from that signal's negative alpha and in direct contradiction to the well-documented debt-issuance/net-external-financing and asset-growth anomalies.

It is a mechanical recombination of two archived signals (the leverage-cheapness wedge and the SIGN(re) gate) built in exactly the archived RANK×SIGN(re) form, and its stated premise misreads the archive — the wedge's +3.22 t-stat contradicted its own negative expected sign, so the "aligned evidence" claim is a post-hoc sign flip rather than new economics.

Debt maturity structure (lct/lt) is a genuinely distinct distress channel from the leverage-level and profitability gates already tested, the expression's direction matches the hypothesis (cheap firms with long-dated obligations long, cheap rollover-risk firms short), and the diagnosis of why prior gates lost alpha to RMW/CMA is a substantive rather than cosmetic motivation.

target_name: Own History Cheapness With Earnings Stock
rationale: Substituting own-history TS_RANK cheapness for cross-sectional B/M is a legitimately different valuation concept with lower HML loading, but the 5-observation TS_RANK is very coarse and, because TS_RANK is non-negative, the composite's sign is entirely driven by re/lt — an Altman-style retained-earnings solvency measure that is close to published territory.

The stated construction claim is factually wrong about the data — non-payers and non-changers give DELTA(dvc)=0, so a large mass of firms sits exactly at zero rather than forming the advertised symmetric raiser/cutter spread — and scaling a dividend flow change by total liabilities is an unmotivated normalization on top of the already-published dividend-change return effect.

(ebitda − pi)/at is dominated by depreciation and amortization, not interest or write-downs, so the expression proxies capital intensity — which loads on investment/CMA and industry composition and contradicts the claimed orthogonality — making the computed quantity a poor match for the stated fixed-charge-coverage hypothesis.
